input.question: Why can extreme hot weather cause mass power outages/blackouts?
input.ground_truth: The main reason is that electricity usage is highest during heat waves, because everyone's air conditioning is running at full blast. There's a second less important reason, which is that fossil fuel and nuclear power plants are less efficient in hot weather. They use outside air and/or water to cool their steam back to water to recycle back into the plant, and that doesn't work as well on a hot day. In fact, it turns out there's a theorem of thermodynamics that says that the maximum possible efficiency of both heat engines (power plant) and refrigerators (air conditioners) is worse when the outside air is warmer. _URL_0_

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why can extreme hot weather cause mass power outages/blackouts?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine it’s a really, really hot day and everyone wants their air conditioner to work so they don’t get too hot. Lots of people turn on their air conditioners at the same time. This makes a big demand for electricity.

Also, when it’s super hot outside, sometimes the big machines that make electricity (called power plants) don’t work as well because they need cool water to make power, and the water gets too warm. Sometimes, the wires that carry electricity can get too hot and sag, which can cause them to break.

So, when too many people want electricity at the same time and the machines or wires can’t handle it, the power can go out for a lot of people. That’s called a blackout or power outage!
